comparisons.peer_topic: RSU vesting and expense recognition policy
comparisons.peer_summary: Granted RSUs predominantly vest over four years and are expensed ratably; those granted to retirement-eligible employees are expensed ratably over the year preceding the grant date.
comparisons.comparison: Both Morgan Stanley and Bank of America disclose that RSU vesting is contingent on continued employment. Morgan Stanley states that RSUs vest 'contingent upon continued employment' and may be forfeited if employment ends before vesting (MS). Bank of America mirrors this requirement, stating that RSUs vest 'provided that the employee remains continuously employed with the Corporation during that time' (BAC). Both firms explicitly link the vesting condition to ongoing employment status.

sentences.text: RSUs are subject to vesting over time, generally one to seven years from the date of award, contingent upon continued employment and subject to restrictions on sale, transfer or assignment until conversion to common stock.
All or a portion of an award may be forfeited if employment is terminated before the end of the relevant vesting period or canceled after the relevant vesting period in certain situations.

The RSUs granted in 2024 and 2023 predominantly vest over four years in one-fourth increments on each of the first four anniversaries of the grant date, provided that the employee remains continuously employed with the Corporation during that time, and will be expensed ratably over the vesting period, net of estimated forfeitures, for non-retirement eligible employees based on the grant-date fair value of the shares.

peer_results.rationale: Candidate disclosures focus on deferred annual incentive awards (diverse settlement methods including cash and cash stock units) rather than standard RSU vesting and dividend rights comparable to the target. While C mentions dividend equivalents for deferred stock awards, the primary topic is settlement mechanisms for deferred compensation rather than standard RSU vesting terms and dividend equivalents for equity awards.

comparisons.peer_topic: Settlement and adjustment terms for performance- or market-condition-based RSUs
comparisons.peer_summary: RSUs subject to performance or market conditions are settled after a three- to five-year period, with awards potentially adjusted from zero to 150% of the original grant based on condition satisfaction, and dividend equivalents paid upon settlement.
comparisons.comparison: Both Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley disclose specific dividend treatment for RSUs upon vesting/settlement. Morgan Stanley states that recipients 'generally receive dividend equivalents if the awards vest' (MS), whereas Goldman Sachs notes that for performance/market-condition RSUs, 'dividend equivalents that accrue on these awards are paid when the awards settle' (GS). Both firms specify that dividend equivalents are realized at the point of vesting/settlement, though GS explicitly ties this to awards subject to performance or market conditions, while MS presents it as a general feature of RSU recipients.

sentences.text: Recipients of RSUs may have voting rights, at the Firm's discretion, and generally receive dividend equivalents if the awards vest.
Dividend equivalents that accrue on these awards are paid when the awards settle.

comparisons.peer_summary: RSUs are granted annually at no cost, generally vesting 50% after two years and 50% after three years, with full-career eligibility provisions and clawback provisions that may result in cancellation. Recipients typically receive cash payments equivalent to dividends during the outstanding period.
comparisons.comparison: Both Morgan Stanley and JPMorgan Chase describe the payment of economic equivalents (dividends) to RSU recipients during the vesting process. Morgan Stanley discloses that recipients 'generally receive dividend equivalents if the awards vest' (MS). JPMorgan Chase similarly states that 'predominantly all RSUs entitle the recipient to receive cash payments equivalent to any dividends paid on the underlying common stock during the period the RSUs are outstanding' (JPM). Both firms provide these dividend equivalents, but JPM explicitly characterizes them as 'cash payments' during the 'outstanding period', whereas MS frames them as being received 'if the awards vest', implying receipt contingent on successful vesting.

sentences.text: Recipients of RSUs may have voting rights, at the Firm's discretion, and generally receive dividend equivalents if the awards vest.
Predominantly all RSUs entitle the recipient to receive cash payments equivalent to any dividends paid on the underlying common stock during the period the RSUs are outstanding.
